randomized_air_hockey.description: Lateral puck interception with randomized launch position (0.10 m window) and speed (1.0-1.5 m/s), the paper's headline generalization setting (Sec. III-A, Fig. 2c right).
randomized_air_hockey.notes: spiking_eprop values are paper-reported: >98% online success after ~1300 of 2000 episodes with 1020 silicon neurons, MuJoCo robot and DYNAP-SE hardware. The gym runs a task-level simulator and a software spiking substrate and scores the final greedy controllers on held-out episodes, so local values are not expected to equal the paper's online rate. The paper reports no hit rate. random_policy and always_forward values are local baselines computed by the evaluator (not paper numbers). Scored protocol: each method submits 10 independently trained controllers (the paper's 10 reservoir seeds); each is executed greedily on 1000 held-out episodes and success is pooled.

success_rate.description: Fraction of held-out episodes, pooled over the five submitted controllers, in which the puck crosses x > 1.5 m with v_x > 0.1 m/s.

seed_worst_success.description: Lowest per-controller success rate among the five independently trained controllers, exposing seed-fragile training.

hit_rate.description: Fraction of held-out episodes with puck-mallet contact, a secondary measure of interception reliability.

controller_units.description: Hidden units of the largest submitted controller, counted from the configuration; above the 1020-unit budget the run fails.

velocity_range_wide.description: Encoding-range scalability: lateral launch speed drawn from the widest main range [0.7, 1.5] m/s with the same 1020-unit budget (Sec. III-B, Fig. 2c left).
velocity_range_wide.notes: spiking_eprop value is the paper-reported ~93% asymptotic online success for the widest main range (down from 97% for [0.7, 0.9] m/s). Local values come from a task-level simulator and software substrate, scored on held-out episodes; the substitute is easier at this range than the paper's robot (local reference ~0.999). random_policy and always_forward values are local evaluator baselines. Scored protocol: each method submits 10 independently trained controllers (the paper's 10 reservoir seeds); each is executed greedily on 1000 held-out episodes and success is pooled.

velocity_range_extreme.description: Where the fixed-size network falls short: launch speed drawn from [0.5, 2.0] m/s with the same 1020-unit budget (Sec. IV, discussion of encoding-range limits).
velocity_range_extreme.notes: spiking_eprop value is the paper-reported 86% success for the [0.5, 2.0] m/s range, which the paper attributes to the finite resolution of a fixed 1020-neuron network (local reference ~0.974). random_policy and always_forward values are local evaluator baselines. Scored protocol: each method submits 10 independently trained controllers (the paper's 10 reservoir seeds); each is executed greedily on 1000 held-out episodes and success is pooled.

single_core_extreme.description: Capacity limit: the [0.5, 2.0] m/s speed range with a 256-unit budget (one DYNAP-SE core) instead of 1020. The paper attributes its wide-range losses to the finite resolution of a fixed-size network and expects more cores to restore performance (Sec. III-B, IV); this experiment measures performance per unit of controller capacity where that limit binds.
single_core_extreme.notes: Not run in the paper: the spiking_eprop value is the local reference (the paper's method and recipe at a quarter of its neuron count, held-out test), not a paper-reported number. Controllers above 256 hidden units fail. random_policy and always_forward values are local evaluator baselines. Scored protocol: each method submits 10 independently trained controllers (the paper's 10 reservoir seeds); each is executed greedily on 1000 held-out episodes and success is pooled.
